en: Mayon Volcano in Albay is famous for its perfectly symmetrical cone shape that you can easily see from Legazpi City.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan flows directly into the sea, making its lower half subject to ocean tides.
Taal Lake in Batangas contains Volcano Island, which itself holds the much smaller Main Crater Lake inside its volcanic cone.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol turn brown during the dry season because the grass covering the mounds dries up.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a sanctuary where divers can observe pristine coral reefs and sea turtles.
Mount Apo in Davao is the highest peak in the Philippines and features observable hot springs and diverse endemic wildlife.
The amihan wind blows from the northeast between November and April, bringing cool and dry weather to most of the Philippines.
Pagsanjan Falls in Laguna is formed by the Pagsanjan River cutting through a deep, narrow gorge with steep rocky walls.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao are carved into the mountainsides, creating giant staircases that catch rainwater for growing rice.
The Philippine tarsier in Bohol has enormous eyes that are larger than its brain, helping it hunt insects at night.
The limestone cliffs of El Nido in Palawan were formed over millions of years from the fossilized remains of marine corals.
Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the Philippines, and its shallow waters often turn green during observable algal blooms.
